reason: The environment's signals are described as guiding cells toward the fibroblast route, matching the goal.
expectation: The signals will guide part of the population toward connective-tissue-producing fibroblasts.

effect: The signals led a subset toward fibroblasts and activated a collagen gene, producing messenger RNA for ribosomes.
reaction: The link from an external signal to a specific gene message is useful, though the mesoderm precursor is unexplained.
reason: Amino acids are the building blocks needed to translate the collagen message into protein.

choice.combine: Developing fibroblasts with collagen messenger RNA

expectation: The fibroblasts will use the amino acids to make a collagen precursor.

effect: The fibroblasts have translated the collagen message into procollagen in the ER and Golgi; the next goal is to build extracellular material.
reaction: The RNA-to-protein connection is clear, though procollagen is not explicitly defined.
reason: The vesicles are shown carrying procollagen from the Golgi to the cell surface, making secretion the next logical step.
expectation: The vesicles will release procollagen outside the fibroblasts.

effect: Procollagen is now outside the fibroblasts, ready for extracellular processing.
reaction: The vesicle-fusion picture makes the secretion step clear.
reason: The enzymes are shown clipping secreted procollagen and linking the resulting collagen molecules.
expectation: The enzymes will process the procollagen into linked collagen fibers.

effect: Processing produced cross-linked collagen fibers that resist tension; hydrated proteoglycans remain to build the extracellular material.
reaction: The opposing arrows make the fibers' tensile role clear.
reason: The proteoglycans are shown as a hydrated gel with spaces for collagen fibers, suggesting they form the remaining extracellular material together.
expectation: The fibers and hydrated gel will form extracellular connective-tissue material.

effect: The collagen fibers and hydrated proteoglycans formed extracellular matrix alongside the fibroblasts, completing the goal.
reaction: The cell-versus-matrix inset is a useful clarification.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the signal from a surface receptor to collagen messenger RNA, then using amino acids to make protein, connected cell specialization to the familiar DNA-to-RNA-to-protein relationship.

leastWorthwhile.text: The development sequence mentions a mesoderm precursor without explaining it; that term could distract students from the otherwise clear signal-to-gene connection.

surprise.text: The final illustration plan explicitly keeps fibroblasts adjacent to the matrix rather than converting them into it, clarifying that cells make material outside themselves.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary: each ingredient's picture suggested its role, though the first result did not explain the mesoderm precursor.

continue.text: I would choose to continue because tracing a gene message through secretion to a material with a physical function made the sequence meaningful. The straightforward combinations left limited scope for difficult decisions, though.
